long_biography.plain_text:
A delayed train from Manchester to London gave J.K. Rowling the idea for Harry Potter in 1990. She spent the next five years mapping the full seven-book sequence, writing longhand and assembling characters, plots and magical rules across scraps of paper before the first novel reached print.

Rowling retained a direct role in extending the fictional world beyond the original books. She collaborated on the stage story Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, wrote the Fantastic Beasts screenplays and launched Pottermore as the series' digital publisher. Companion books also channelled royalties to charitable work, including Lumos, the children's organisation she founded and leads.
